title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Robert Half Talent Solutions are seeking a permanent Management Accountant to join a fast paced private equity backed business in Newport

We are seeking a proactive Part-Qualified Management Accountant to join our fast-paced finance team. This role offers a unique blend of core management accounting, commercial analysis, and high-level exposure to board-level reporting. You will play a critical role in maintaining the integrity of our financial data while supporting the business through a period of PE-driven growth.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Accounting & Month-End
- Management Accounts: Preparation and assistance with monthly management accounts, including prepayments, balance sheet reconciliations, and all relevant month-end tasks.
- Fixed Assets & Stock: Full ownership of Fixed Assets, including maintaining the register. Responsible for Creditors and Stock management, including weekly and month-end reporting.
- Ledger Management: Daily bank reconciliations, postings, and allocations to the AR/AP ledgers.
- Purchase Ledger Support: Ensuring all manual and 3-way match GRN invoices are processed accurately and timely, in accordance with company finance policies.

Reporting & Board Exposure
- Presentations: Assist in preparation and delivery of both Board presentations and Budget presentations.
- Group & International: Assisting with group consolidations and the management of International accounts.
- Cash Management: Managing the weekly payment run and providing essential assistance with cashflow forecasting.

Commercial Analysis & Budgeting
- Budgeting: Assisting with the preparation of annual budgets.
- Variance Analysis: Reviewing weekly, bi-weekly, and monthly spend with budget holders to analyse and report on spend vs. variance.

Audit & Compliance
- Statutory Requirements: Assist in the preparation for Statutory returns and assisting in the year-end Statutory Audit.
- External Liaison: Assist with External Audits.

Candidate Profile
- Technical Skills: Strong ERP experience and advanced Excel skills. Understanding of double entry and reconciliations
- Communication: Confident in presenting financial data to senior leadership and collaborating with non-finance budget holders.

What We Offer
- Full study support package
- Exposure to Private Equity reporting cycles and high-level board interaction.
- Salary from £30,000 to £35,000
- Hybrid working-
- Company bonus scheme

Robert Half Ltd acts as an employment business for temporary positions and an employment agency for permanent positions. Robert Half is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. Suitable candidates with equivalent qualifications and more or less experience can apply. Rates of pay and salary ranges are dependent upon your experience, qualifications and training. title: Accounts Administration Assistant
description:
12-Month Fixed-Term Contract

A fantastic opportunity has arisen to join the finance shared services team of a highly successful global organisation operating within a fast-paced, technology-led environment.

This 12-month fixed-term position has been created to support the continued growth of the European Shared Service Centre and offers the chance to become part of a collaborative finance team supporting multiple international business entities.

The Role

As a Travel & Expense (T&E) Administrator, you will be responsible for ensuring the accurate and timely audit of employee travel and expense claims, providing support with payment activities, and delivering excellent customer service to stakeholders across the business.

Working within a dedicated team, you will help maintain compliance with company policies, resolve employee queries and contribute to the smooth operation of the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Auditing travel and expense submissions in line with company policies and internal controls
- Reviewing and resolving employee and stakeholder queries relating to expenses and financial transactions
- Supporting regular payment runs across multiple entities
- Assisting with month-end and year-end finance processes
- Supporting the preparation of financial reports and documentation
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner
- Maintaining employee data in accordance with data protection requirements
- Working closely with colleagues and other departments to support efficient financial operations
- Contributing to process improvements, training and knowledge-sharing activities
- Supporting wider shared service centre activities as required
- Occasional travel to support finance projects and system implementations

Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will ideally possess:
- Previous experience within a transactional finance environment
- Experience using a Travel & Expense platform such as Concur, Chrome River or SAP
- ERP system experience, with SAP highly desirable
- Strong Microsoft Excel and Office skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Effective communication and stakeholder management abilities
- A proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills
- The ability to work independently and collaboratively
- A positive, customer-focused mindset

Qualifications
- Prior experience in finance administration, accounts payable or transactional finance preferred
- AAT studies or qualification would be advantageous but are not essential

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Annual bonus opportunity
- Flexible and hybrid working arrangements
- Exposure to a global finance function within a growing international organisation
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to contribute to ongoing finance transformation projects

Location

This is a hybrid position based in South Wales. Following an initial training period of approximately 12 weeks, the role will operate on a 3 days office / 2 days home working basis.

title: Warranty Administrator
company: Perfect Placement Uk Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing the warranty process across three franchises, supporting a team of five Service Advisors. This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced automotive professional seeking a long-term career with a well-established dealership group operating throughout South West England and South Wales.

Benefits for the successful Warranty Administrator:
- Salary up to £30,000 per annum, dependent on experience
- Performance-based bonus scheme
- 22 days' annual holiday plus 8 bank holidays
- Discounted car purchase programme for you and your family
- Cycle to work scheme
- Healthcare provisions and hospitality/event perks
- Excellent career progression opportunities within a large, reputable dealership group
- Monday to Friday working hours, 8:30am to 5:00pm, with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break

Duties of the Warranty Administrator:
- Preparing and submitting warranty claims to manufacturers for payment
- Checking weekly statements, querying overdue claims, and resolving discrepancies
- Ensuring warranty documentation aligns with manufacturer guidelines
- Preparing accurate invoices and warranty claims, managing open times and job card write-ups
- Completing repair order documentation accurately and comprehensively
- Ensuring all policy claims are processed promptly and reimbursements are correct
- Maintaining control over returned displaced material
- Reconciling warranty credits and resolving discrepancies efficiently

Requirements of the Warranty Administrator:

title: Facilities Co-ordinator
description:

You'll be the central point of contact for a wide range of facilities-related matters, working closely with colleagues, suppliers, contractors, and landlords to keep our offices running smoothly.

- Co-ordinate facilities maintenance and repairs across multiple office locations.
- Liaise with contractors, suppliers, landlords, and service providers.
- Manage facilities-related enquiries and requests.
- Arrange planned maintenance and monitor completion of works.
- Support office moves, workplace improvements, and office set-up activities.
- Maintain facilities records, documentation, and supplier information.
- Assist with health and safety compliance requirements.
- Monitor facilities expenditure and process supplier invoices where required.
- Build effective relationships with colleagues across the business.

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in facilities, office management, or a similar role.
- Good understanding of health & safety laws and regulations.
- Excellent organisational and administrative skills.
- Strong communication and relationship-building abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
- A proactive, practical, and solutions-focused approach.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to delivering excellent service.
- Someone willing and able to work 24 hours per week across 3 or 4 days.

Why Join Acorn by Synergie?

Benefits include:
- Minimum 33 days' holiday pro-rata.
- Your birthday off and a You Day.
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).
- Company pension scheme.
- Life assurance from day one.
- Friendly and supportive working environment.
- Paid time off to support the local community.

title: Payroll Administrator
company: Richmond Accountancy Services Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job description:

About the role

We are looking for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join our team at Richmond Accountancy Services Limited in Abergavenny.

This is a full-time, office-based position and would suit someone who already has practical experience running payrolls and is looking to develop their career within a friendly, established accountancy practice.

You will be responsible for managing payrolls for a portfolio of clients, covering businesses of different sizes and pay frequencies.

Key responsibilities

Your role will include:
- Processing weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls
- Calculating salaries, wages, overtime, holiday pay, statutory payments and deductions
- Processing starters and leavers
- Preparing and submitting RTI returns to HMRC
- Managing workplace pension and auto-enrolment requirements
- Processing pension contributions and submissions to pension providers
- Dealing with payroll queries from clients and employees
- Preparing payroll reports, payslips and other relevant documentation
- Keeping payroll records accurate and up to date
- Ensuring payroll deadlines are met
- Liaising with HMRC and pension providers where required

Experience we're looking for

Previous hands-on payroll experience is essential. You should be comfortable managing payrolls and working to regular deadlines with a high level of accuracy.

Experience with IRIS Elements Payroll would be preferred, although this is not essential. We are very happy to consider applicants who have experience using other payroll software.

Experience dealing with workplace pensions and auto-enrolment is also important.

We're looking for someone who is organised, reliable and comfortable communicating directly with clients.

Qualifications & development

Formal payroll or accountancy qualifications are not essential if you have the right practical experience.

For someone who would like to gain further relevant professional qualifications, we are happy to support your development and fund appropriate qualifications and training.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their payroll career while gaining further qualifications alongside their role.

What we offer
- Salary of £28,000 per year
- Full-time, permanent position
- Employer-funded professional qualifications and training
- Opportunity for continued professional development
- Varied portfolio of payroll clients
- Friendly and supportive accountancy practice environment
- Office-based role in Abergavenny

Working arrangements

Job type: Full-time, Permanent

Salary: £28,000 per year

Location: Abergavenny

Work location: In person

If you have previous payroll experience and are looking for a role where you can take responsibility for client payrolls while continuing to develop your skills and qualifications, we'd be pleased to hear from you.

Apply with your CV and a brief covering note outlining your payroll experience.

title: QC Administrator
description:
Administrators - Why You Should Apply

A new career, no degree needed: You don't need a lab or science background to become a QC Administrator here. Everything is fully trained, so if you've got sharp admin skills and an eye for detail, this is your way into the science sector without going back to university.

Build your day around you: Flexitime lets you start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am and finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm. Do the school run, beat the traffic, or get to the gym while it's quiet, then shape your hours around your life.

Grow with a busy lab: New business is coming in fast, and the small team is set to expand, so you're joining at the point where there's real room to move up.

Your salary, benefits & hours of work
- 27,000 and annual bonus
- Flexitime: start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am, finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm
- Monday to Friday, no weekends
- Full training from day one
- No weekend or bank holiday working, with a shutdown from Christmas to the New Year.
- Holidays 24 days plus 8 Bank Holidays (increasing with length of service - one extra day for every 5 years to a maximum of 25 years)

What you'll do as the QC Administrator

You'll keep the Quality Control project team running smoothly, handling the admin that gets samples tested and results back to customers.
- Book stability and project samples into the QC systems
- Organise despatch of samples to partner testing laboratories, raising purchase orders and labelling correctly
- Collect and trend data, create Certificates of Analysis and draft customer quotes
- Complete and archive records, keeping the lab audit-ready
- Prepare reagents and run basic sample checks once trained
- Order consumables and support improvements across the lab

What you'll need to apply for the QC Administrator
- Strong, hands-on administration experience with a genuine eye for detail
- Good computer literacy (Microsoft Office 365) and happy to learn new systems.

Interested?

title: HR Assistant
description:
Quick Staff UK is recruiting for an HR Assistant to join an established manufacturing business in the Tredegar area.

This is a varied, hands-on HR role, working directly with the HR Manager and providing support across recruitment, employee relations, absence management, HR administration and the wider employee lifecycle. Job Description HR Assistant

Importantly, this isn't a role where you'll necessarily remain an HR Assistant long term. The company is keen to support the successful candidate in developing their HR knowledge, taking on greater responsibility and progressing towards a broader HR Officer / HR Generalist position as their experience develops. Job Description HR Assistant

Hours of Work

Monday to Thursday: 8:30am 5:00pm with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break
Friday: 8:30am 2:30pm with no lunch break

Alternatively, on Friday you can work 8:00am 2:30pm with a 30-minute lunch break.

The position is 37.5 hours per week and fully site-based, with an early finish every Friday.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Acting as a first point of contact for day-to-day HR queries
- Supporting the HR Manager with employee relations matters
- Assisting with reviewing and updating HR policies and procedures
- Supporting maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental leave, flexible working and other HR processes
- Monitoring absence and supporting managers with the absence management process
- Maintaining accurate employee records and updating the HR system
- Producing information and reports for payroll, production and HR
- Supporting temporary and permanent recruitment, including advertising vacancies, CV screening, interviews and onboarding
- Supporting the complete employee lifecycle, from recruitment and induction through to leavers
- Assisting with training and development administration
- Supporting performance management processes
- Helping with employee engagement, health and wellbeing initiatives
- Providing additional HR administrative support as required

The role will also provide exposure to recruitment, employee relations, capability, absence and performance management, with the opportunity to gradually take ownership of HR processes. Job Description HR Assistant

What We're Looking For

Ideally, you'll already have at least two years' experience within an HR administrative role and be ready for the next stage in your HR career.

You'll ideally have:
- Working knowledge of current UK employment legislation
- Experience supporting employee relations administration
- Recruitment experience
- Experience with absence management and HR processes
- Exposure to performance management administration
- Strong HR administration and record-keeping skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- High attention to detail
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information professionally
- Good organisational and interpersonal skills
- Confidence using Microsoft Office

Experience within a manufacturing environment would be beneficial but isn't essential. Experience using an HRIS would also be advantageous. A relevant HR qualification or CIPD Level 3 or above is desirable. Job Description HR Assistant

Why Apply?

This could be a particularly good opportunity if you're currently working as an HR Administrator or HR Assistant and want a position where you can develop beyond administration.

You'll work closely with an experienced HR Manager, gain broader exposure to HR matters and have the opportunity to develop towards an HR Officer / Generalist role as your knowledge and confidence grow.
- Salary: £30,000 per annum
- 37.5 hours per week
- Early finish every Friday
- Permanent, on-site position
- ASAP start
